This is an incredibly dark story that may end better, but the cut scenes are full of the player characters constantly bickering and there is a moment where you are not able to have any agency as the parents of this poor child (and thus the players controlling them) destroy something very precious to their child little by little as she cries for the parents (and thus you as the player controlling them) to stop. This is not a cut scene you can walk away from. This is forced to be actively done and the only other option is for the **players** to walk away.

The gameplay between terrible story beats is good. It's staggering how well you and your friend or partner can have a great time cooperating to the next story beat just to have the characters constantly devolve back to bickering and blaming as soon as the current challenge is completed. Even if they decide to stay together after the experience, it will only last until something goes wrong again.

The gameplay, design, creativity, and environment were all excellent but even so I had a hard time giving this game a positive review. Why? Because the main characters are complete psychopaths! They have no concept of mercy, or kindness their instinctual response to any sort of adversity is murder and destruction. Their bloodlust is such that they are willing to torturously murder innocent creatures begging for their own lives.

Regarding characters that they didnt brutally murder, for a game about fixing a relationship the characters are incredibly cavalier about the mental health and emotional well being of any other characters in the game including their own daughter.

At the start of the game the characters were unpleasant, however you expect that to moderate or change through the story on their path to reconciliation, but they dont get better, if anything they get worse. About half way through the game there is a scene which made one of my friends quit and refuse to continue playing, and while I continued through to the end, my sympathy for the characters was completely erased.

Other than that, the game was great! The environments were very detailed and beautiful, the gameplay was innovative and the incorporation of various household objects as platforming or environmental puzzles was refreshingly creative.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Review: It Takes Two is hands down one of the best co-op games out there. From start to finish, it’s packed with fun, crazy creative levels, and mechanics that keep changing so it never gets boring. You and your partner will be solving puzzles, platforming, and facing off against quirky enemies, and you'll need to work together the entire time.

The story’s surprisingly emotional too—Cody and May are trying to save their marriage, but it’s told with a lot of humor, so it’s not heavy. The game’s beautiful, with colorful, unique worlds that are just awesome to explore.

The coolest part? You have to cooperate. Each of you has different abilities, so you really need to communicate and help each other out. It’s challenging, but super satisfying when you figure it all out.

If you're looking for an amazing co-op experience, this game is a no-brainer. You’ll laugh, yell at each other (in a good way!), and have a blast from start to finish.

Pros:
- Really fun idea for a game.
- Beautiful and interesting environments.
- Great cooperative gameplay.
- Often enjoyable banter between the player characters.*

* - But the characters are supposed to have marital troubles...

Cons:
- Poor writing.**
- Terrible unresponsiveness with many of the controls for abilities and minigames.
- Occasional camera issues where it would not move for a second and then suddenly move; very disorienting.
- Small amount of graphical lag/jittering, especially during cutscenes.
- Rare game freezing that requires force closing and restarting the game.

** - This game is more about the experience than the story. It plays out like a child wrote the storyline while an adult (with little knowledge about divorces) wrote the script. The more you distance yourself from the story, the better you'll feel playing it, especially during particularly dreadful moments. (See spoiler below.)
